mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS rate change (p > 0.05 in OLS regression).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and equity valuations, producing positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 2% in a month while UNRATE decreases by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: In a labor strengthening regime, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05 in a regression controlling for macro variables).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) relative to GDP (implied by INDPRO) indicates excess demand in the economy, prompting market participants to price in higher future corporate profits and equity valuations, leading to positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 grows by > 3% quarter-on-quarter while INDPRO remains flat or grows < 1%
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is negative despite the signal (p < 0.05 in a two-tailed test).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) over two consecutive months suggests supply-side constraints, reducing expected future earnings and pushing down S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines by > 5% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant negative relationship between INDPRO declines and 20-day forward returns (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly increases by more than 0.3% in a month, market participants anticipate future rate cuts, which lowers discount rates and supports equity valuations, producing a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is not positive when the CPIAUCSL surprise exceeds +0.3% (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period of declining labor participation rate proxies (not available in the given catalog; use HOUST as a labor proxy) coupled with rising job openings (not available) would imply weak labor markets, but since only HOUST is available, we use it as a proxy for underemployment, producing negative 20-day returns when HOUST falls sharply.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases by > 10% over two consecutive months
failure_condition: A sharp HOUST decline does not result in a statistically significant negative 20-day forward return (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising unemployment (UNRATE) and stable industrial production (INDPRO) indicate a supply-side imbalance favoring deflationary pressures, which depresses equity valuations and yields negative 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by > 0.4% while INDPRO remains unchanged for two months
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05 in a two-tailed test).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden surge in retail sales proxies (not available) or a sharp rise in consumer confidence indices (not available) would typically drive equity returns, but using HOUST as a proxy for consumer demand, a rapid increase in HOUST suggests optimism and positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by > 15% in a single month
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not positive when HOUST spikes (p > 0.05).
